To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) diameter growth in partially cut stands was greater than in uncut controls, and diameter growth in the partially-cut stands was sufficient for the stands to reach the susceptibility threshold in <25 years; and (2) basal area growth in the partially-cuts stands was sufficient to reach the susceptibility basal area threshold in <25 to 35 years, but windthrow in GSL 40 stands reduced basal area and delayed stand susceptibility.
partially cut stands of 30- to 40-year-old lodgepole pine are not likely to reach the basal areas required for mountain pine beetle attack for at least 25-50 years.
